definitions.definition: Torus=reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi). Periodic spatial products, integrals and derivatives are on this torus. A trigonometric polynomial is a finite sum of exp(i*k*x) with integer k.

For a periodic integrable f, hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x)exp(-i*k*x) dx, k in Z. Extend Fourier coefficients to periodic distributions. Reality means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0. For sequences, ell^2 is the square-summable sequence space with counting measure.

definitions.type: family of real or complex Hilbert spaces indexed by real order
definitions.definition: Write <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_{k in Z}<k>^(2s)|hat f(k)|^2, interpreted as distributions for s<0. L^2=H^0 and ||.||_2 denotes its normalized norm. For mean-zero f, ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_{k!=0}|k|^(2s)|hat f(k)|^2. For s>=0, ||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s); for s<0, 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=||f||_(dot H^s). In time L^infty norms are essential suprema, replaced by ordinary suprema for continuous representatives; derivative norms remain essential suprema.

definitions.type: averaged covariance of two real phases
definitions.definition: For tau>0, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s)ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
For integers a,b,c and k=a+b+c, set p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3.

For nonzero integers a,b,c,d with a+b+c+d=0, let N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the decreasing rearrangement of |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|, resolving ties in any order. Nthird(a,b,c,d)=N3. Thus N3 is the second smallest of all four magnitudes including the dual output.

definitions.type: family of trilinear Fourier operators initially on mean-zero trigonometric polynomials
definitions.definition: For tau>0, real base time t_n and k!=0, hat R2_(t_n,tau)(f1,f2,f3)(k)=-(tau/(18*i*k))*sum_{a+b+c=k,a+b!=0}exp(-i*t_n*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), with zero coefficient at k=0; Phase gives alpha,beta,Phi. Write R2^n_tau for t_n=n*tau. Bounded extensions, when used, are proved below.

inputs.statement: For tau>0 and real alpha,beta, eta_tau(alpha,beta)=0 if alpha*beta=0; otherwise |eta_tau|<=2*min(|alpha/beta|,|beta/alpha|) and |eta_tau|<=tau*min(|alpha|,|beta|). For every nonzero integer quadruple a+b+c+d=0, N1<=3*N2 and, writing A=|ab|, B0=|cd|, one has (1/|d|)*min(A/B0,B0/A)<=3/Nthird(a,b,c,d), and |a+b|/max(A,B0)<=6/Nthird(a,b,c,d).

There is an absolute C such that for all nonnegative x1,x2,x3,x4 in ell^2(Z\{0}), sum_{a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0} x1(a)x2(b)x3(c)x4(d)/Nthird(a,b,c,d)<=C*product_{j=1}^4||xj||_(ell^2). The sum is the supremum of finite positive partial sums; the same bound holds when it is restricted to any subset of quadruples.

output.statement: For 0<=sigma<=1, tau>0, any real base time a, and mean-zero fj in H^sigma, ||R2_(a,tau)(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_j||fj||_(H^sigma), uniformly in a,tau and Fourier support. The bound holds after inserting any multiplier of modulus <=1, including restriction to Phi=0 or Phi!=0. Polynomial approximation defines its unique continuous trilinear extension. Moreover, for 0<gamma<=1, mean-zero w in H^gamma with ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M, f in mean-zero L^2, delta=||f-w||_2<=1 and 0<tau<=1, ||R2_(a,tau)(f,f,f)||_2<=C_(M,gamma)*tau*(tau^gamma+delta). This estimate requires no H^gamma bound on f.

argument.text: Fix sigma,tau,a0,f1,f2,f3 and assume L1: 0<=sigma<=1, tau>0, and each f_j is mean-zero in H^sigma. Initially take polynomial inputs. In a nonzero term set k=a+b+c, p=a+b and d=-k. Terms with a zero input, k=0 or p=0 vanish or are excluded; if a phase is zero eta vanishes. For the remaining terms set A=|ab|, B0=|cd|, so the ratio of |alpha| and |beta| is the ratio of A and B0. N003 therefore gives |eta|/|k|<=6/Nthird. Its other covariance bound gives |eta|/(tau*|abck|)<=3*|p|*min(A,B0)/(A*B0)=3*|p|/max(A,B0)<=18/Nthird. Interpolating these two numerical inequalities with powers 1-sigma and sigma gives |eta|/(|k|*|abc|^sigma)<=6^(1-sigma)*18^sigma*tau^sigma/Nthird. All constants here are independent of the base time.

produces.statement: For every contributing nonzero frequency triple r1,r2,r3 with k0=r1+r2+r3!=0 and r1+r2!=0, and phases alpha0=3*r1*r2*(r1+r2), beta0=3*k0*r3*(r1+r2), one has |eta_tau(alpha0,beta0)|/(|k0|*|r1*r2*r3|^sigma)<=6^(1-sigma)*18^sigma*tau^sigma/Nthird(r1,r2,r3,-k0).

argument.text: Dualize the R2 Fourier sum against any finitely supported ell^2 sequence of norm one and take absolute values. Use N004 with x1(a)=|a|^sigma|hat f1(a)|, x2(b)=|b|^sigma|hat f2(b)|, x3(c)=|c|^sigma|hat f3(c)| and x4(d)=the absolute value of the dual coefficient at -d. The first three ell^2 norms are bounded by the H^sigma norms. The factors exp(-i*a0*Phi) have modulus one. With the prefactor tau/18, F001 and N004 give C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product||fj||_(H^sigma). The same absolute-envelope argument allows any inserted multiplier of modulus <=1 and any subset of frequencies, including either total-phase restriction.

produces.statement: For polynomial mean-zero inputs and 0<=sigma<=1, ||R2_(a0,tau)(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*tau^(1+sigma)*product_j||fj||_(H^sigma); the same bound holds after any multiplier of modulus <=1 is inserted in its Fourier sum.

argument.text: Approximate each input by its Fourier truncations in H^sigma. Trilinearity and F002 bound every telescoping difference by a sum of one vanishing norm times two bounded norms. Thus the outputs are Cauchy in complete L^2, independent of the approximations, and define the claimed continuous extension and bound. At nonzero fixed output the coefficient is the same continuous limit of the polynomial formula. Discharge L1 and quantify these inputs.

produces.statement: For every rho in [0,1], positive step s0, real base b0 and mean-zero inputs g1,g2,g3 in H^rho, ||R2_(b0,s0)(g1,g2,g3)||_2<=C_rho*s0^(1+rho)*product_j||gj||_(H^rho). The same estimate holds after any multiplier of modulus <=1 is inserted in the Fourier sum, and polynomial approximation defines its continuous trilinear extension.

argument.text: For the numerical-state assertion fix w,f,M and assume L2: w is mean-zero H^gamma, ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M, f is mean-zero L^2, delta=||f-w||_2<=1 and 0<tau<=1. H002 supplies 0<gamma<=1. Apply F003 at sigma=gamma to (w,w,w). Expand the difference at (f,f,f) by trilinearity, for example R2(f-w,f,f)+R2(w,f-w,f)+R2(w,w,f-w), and use F003 at sigma=0 in every term. Since ||f||_2<=M+1, the difference is <=C*tau*delta*(||f||_2+||w||_2)^2. Adding the exact-data bound gives C_(M,gamma)*tau*(tau^gamma+delta). Discharge L2 and quantify; no numerical Sobolev norm entered.
